new.name: Parachute Adams
new.creator_name: Adams by Leonard Halladay (1922); parachute style
new.description: The most versatile dry fly there is: grizzly and brown hackle tails, a grey dubbed body and a white post you can see in any light.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it whenever small grey or brown mayflies or midges are about, or as a searching dry. The post makes it easy to follow in riffles.
mats: White calf body hair or poly yarn
Mixed brown and grizzly hackle fibres
Brown and grizzly cock, wound parachute
steps: Tie in a post of white calf hair or poly a third back from the eye, stand it up with thread wraps in front and around its base.
Tie in a tail of mixed brown and grizzly fibres, about a shank length.
Dub a slim, tapered grey body up to the post.
Tie in the two hackles at the post, dub a little thorax around it.
Wind the hackles around the post, one at a time, working down the post; tie off in front.
Whip finish under the hackle and trim the post to length.
new.imitates: Mayfly duns (blue-winged olives, March browns, Callibaetis) and adult midges
new.hatch: All season; especially spring and autumn mayfly hatches

new.name: Elk Hair Caddis
new.description: Al Troth's classic adult caddis: a dubbed body palmered with brown hackle, ribbed with fine wire, under a flared elk hair wing.
new.fishing_tips: Skate or twitch it across riffles in the evening, or dead-drift it. A great dry to hang a nymph under.
steps: Tie in the wire at the bend and dub a body to just short of the eye.
Tie in a brown hackle at the front and palmer it back to the bend in open turns.
Wind the wire forward through the hackle to lock it down, wiggling it; trim the hackle tip.
Clean and stack a bunch of elk hair, measure to the bend and tie it in with tight wraps so it flares.
Whip finish behind the hair, then trim the butts square to form the head.

new.name: Royal Wulff
new.description: The famous high-floating attractor: moose tail, peacock herl and red floss body, white calf wings and a brown hackle.
new.fishing_tips: A rough-water searching fly that floats all day; great in pocket water and for brook trout.
mats: White calf body or tail hair, divided
Peacock herl / red floss / peacock herl
steps: Tie in a bunch of white calf hair, upright and divided into two wings, a third back from the eye.
Tie in a tail of moose hair, as long as the shank.
Wind a band of peacock herl, then a band of red floss, then another band of peacock herl up to the wings.
Tie in two brown hackles and wind them behind and in front of the wings.
Form a neat head and whip finish.
new.imitates: General attractor; suggests big mayflies, caddis or terrestrials
new.hatch: Summer and early autumn, especially in pocket water

new.name: Stimulator
new.description: A buoyant stonefly and caddis imitation: elk hair tail and wing, palmered abdomen, and an orange or yellow thorax with grizzly hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it as a high-floating dry in riffles and pocket water, alone or with a nymph underneath.
mats: Yellow or orange dubbing, palmered with brown hackle
steps: Tie in a short elk hair tail, then the wire and a brown hackle at the bend.
Dub the abdomen two-thirds up the shank, palmer the hackle forward and rib with the wire.
Tie in an elk hair wing reaching the tail end.
Tie in a grizzly hackle, dub an orange thorax, and palmer the hackle through it.
Whip finish.
new.imitates: Stoneflies (golden stones, yellow sallies) and large caddis
new.hatch: Late spring to autumn; goldens in early summer

new.name: Griffith's Gnat
new.description: Just a peacock herl body palmered with grizzly hackle: a tiny midge cluster that trout sip in flat water.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it when trout are sipping midges in slow water and nothing else works.
steps: Tie in the wire, a grizzly hackle and one or two peacock herls at the bend.
Wind the herl to the eye and tie off.
Palmer the hackle forward in open turns and tie off.
Rib the wire through the hackle to protect the herl; whip finish.
new.hatch: All year, especially winter and on calm, flat water

new.name: Chernobyl Ant
new.creator_name: Mark Forslund and Allan Woolley (Green River, Utah)
new.description: A big, unsinkable foam terrestrial with rubber legs and a bright indicator, good enough to suspend a nymph.
new.fishing_tips: Slap it down near banks in summer and let it drift; twitch occasionally. Works on bass and bluegill too.
mats: Orange or yellow foam or yarn
steps: Wrap a short dubbed or chenille underbody so the foam has something to grip.
Lay the foam strip on top and tie it down in two or three segments.
Tie a pair of rubber legs on each side at each segment.
Tie a small indicator tuft on top at the front segment.
Whip finish under the foam and trim the legs.
new.imitates: Beetles, crickets, large ants and hoppers

new.name: Sparkle Dun
new.description: A Comparadun with a sparkling Z-Lon shuck: a deer hair fan wing over a slim dubbed body, riding low in the film like a hatching mayfly.
new.fishing_tips: Match the colour to the hatch (PMD, BWO, Trico) and fish it to rising trout on smooth water.
mats: Fine dubbing to match the hatch
steps: Stack and tie in a bunch of comparadun hair a third back from the eye, tips forward, and trim the butts at an angle.
Tie in a short Z-Lon shuck at the bend.
Dub a slim body forward to the wing.
Push the wing upright with thread wraps in front and dub around it so it fans out in a half circle.
Whip finish.
new.imitates: Emerging mayfly duns (PMDs, BWOs, sulphurs, Tricos)
new.hatch: Spring to autumn, during mayfly hatches

new.name: Parachute Hopper
new.description: A realistic but simple grasshopper: dubbed body, turkey wing, knotted legs and a parachute hackle around a visible post.
new.fishing_tips: Bang it against grassy banks on windy summer afternoons.
steps: Tie in a post of poly yarn a third back from the eye.
Dub a full body over the rear two-thirds.
Tie a coated turkey wing on top, tent-shaped over the body, and a knotted leg on each side.
Tie in the hackle at the post, dub the thorax, wind the hackle parachute-style and tie off.
Whip finish.

new.name: Flashback Pheasant Tail
new.description: Sawyer's pheasant tail nymph with a bead, a peacock thorax and a pearl flashback over the wing case.
new.fishing_tips: Dead-drift it under an indicator or as the point fly on a Euro rig. One of the most reliable mayfly nymphs anywhere.
steps: Slide on the bead and start the thread behind it.
Tie in a few pheasant tail fibres as a short tail, keeping the butts long, and tie in the wire.
Wrap the pheasant fibres up two-thirds of the shank as the body and rib with the wire.
Tie in pearl flash and the remaining pheasant fibres on top, then wrap a peacock herl thorax.
Pull the wing case over, tie down, fold the fibre tips back as legs, and whip finish behind the bead.
new.imitates: Mayfly nymphs (Baetis and other swimmers and crawlers)
new.hatch: All season; best before and during mayfly hatches

new.name: Zebra Midge
new.description: About as simple as flies get: a black thread body ribbed with silver wire and a silver bead.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it deep under an indicator in tailwaters and stillwaters, especially in winter.
steps: Slide on the bead and start the thread behind it.
Tie in the wire and wrap it down into the bend.
Build a slim, slightly tapered thread body back up to the bead.
Rib with the wire in even turns, tie off, and whip finish behind the bead.
new.hatch: All year; most valuable in winter on tailwaters

new.name: Copper John
new.description: A heavy, flashy attractor nymph: goose biot tail, copper wire body, peacock thorax, flashback wing case and partridge legs.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it deep as the point fly in fast riffles, or as the dropper under a big dry.
mats: Thin Skin with pearl flash, epoxy-coated
steps: Add the bead and a few turns of lead-free wire, pushed into the bead.
Tie in two goose biots, split, as the tail.
Wrap the copper wire body in touching turns up two-thirds of the shank.
Tie in the Thin Skin and flash on top, wrap a peacock herl thorax, and tie hen fibres along each side as legs.
Pull the wing case over, tie off, whip finish and coat the wing case with epoxy or UV resin.
new.imitates: Stonefly and mayfly nymphs; also an attractor
new.hatch: All season, especially spring and summer in riffles

new.name: Prince Nymph
new.description: The famous attractor nymph: brown biot tail, peacock herl body ribbed with gold, white biot wings and a brown hackle collar.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it dead-drift under an indicator, or swing it like a wet fly.
steps: Add the bead and tie in two brown biots as a forked tail.
Tie in the tinsel and peacock herl, wind the herl body forward and rib it.
Wind two or three turns of brown hen as a collar.
Tie two white biots flat on top, curving outward, as wings.
Whip finish behind the bead.
new.imitates: Stonefly or caddis nymphs; a general attractor

new.name: Frenchie
new.description: A pheasant tail nymph with a hot pink or orange collar, tied on a jig hook with a tungsten bead for Euro nymphing.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it on a tight-line Euro rig in riffles and runs; it bounces bottom without snagging.
mats: Hot pink or orange UV dubbing
steps: Slide on the bead and add a few wraps of lead-free wire if you want more weight.
Tie in a short Coq de Leon tail and the wire.
Wrap a pheasant tail body and rib it with the wire.
Dub a small hot-spot collar of pink or orange behind the bead.
Whip finish.

new.name: Pat's Rubber Legs
new.description: A weighted chenille stonefly with rubber legs and tails: simple, durable and one of the best big nymphs there is.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it deep under an indicator in fast water, often with a small nymph trailed behind.
steps: Wrap lead-free wire over the middle of the shank and cover it with thread.
Tie in a pair of rubber legs at the bend as the tails, and the chenille.
Wind the chenille forward a third, tie in a set of legs each side; repeat twice more.
Finish the chenille behind the eye, tie in short antennae if you like, and whip finish.
new.hatch: All year; especially spring before the stonefly hatch

new.name: San Juan Worm
new.description: A single strip of red or pink Vernille tied on a curved hook with the ends flamed to taper them.
new.fishing_tips: Deadly after rain and in rising, coloured water when worms wash in. Carp and panfish eat it too.
mats: Red, pink or wine Vernille (ultra chenille)
steps: Lightly flame both ends of a 2-inch piece of Vernille to taper them.
Lay a thread base and tie the Vernille on top at the middle of the shank.
Wrap the thread forward around the Vernille to the front and back again to secure it.
Whip finish; the ends stick out front and back like a worm.
new.hatch: All year, especially after rain and in high water

new.name: Pink Squirrel
new.description: A Driftless favourite: crystal flash tail, squirrel dubbing body ribbed with wire, and a pink chenille collar behind a gold bead.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it under an indicator on spring creeks; the pink collar is the trigger.
mats: Pearl Krystal Flash or brown fibres
Pink UV chenille or Ice Dub
steps: Add the bead and tie in a short tail and the wire.
Dub a squirrel body two-thirds up the shank and rib it.
Wrap two turns of pink chenille or a pink dubbed collar behind the bead.
Pick out the body fibres for legs and whip finish.
new.imitates: Scuds, cressbugs and mayfly nymphs; an attractor

new.name: RS2
new.description: Rim Chung's tiny Baetis emerger: split microfibbet tails, a slim dubbed body and a short wing of CDC or poly.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it in the film or just under it during a BWO hatch, or as a dropper below a dry.
mats: Grey CDC or white poly, short
steps: Tie in two microfibbets as a split tail.
Dub a slim, tapered body to two-thirds of the shank.
Tie in a short tuft of CDC or poly on top as the emerging wing.
Dub a tiny thorax around it and whip finish.

new.name: Walt's Worm
new.description: A dead-simple buggy nymph: hare's ear dubbing over a weighted jig hook with a tungsten bead. Suggests a cranefly larva, scud or caddis.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it deep on a Euro rig; it's a top searching nymph when nothing is hatching.
steps: Slide on the bead and start the thread behind it.
Dub a carrot-shaped body of hare's ear from the bend to the bead.
Rib it if you like, whip finish, and rough it up with velcro.

new.name: Mickey Finn
new.description: A bright yellow-red-yellow bucktail over a silver tinsel body: a classic attractor streamer.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it fast for stocked trout, bass and pickerel, especially in coloured water.
mats: A few strands of gold flash (optional)
steps: Wrap a flat silver tinsel body and rib it with oval tinsel.
Tie in a small bunch of yellow bucktail on top, reaching just past the bend.
Add a bunch of red bucktail on top of that, then a larger bunch of yellow on top.
Build a neat black head, whip finish and varnish.

new.name: Slumpbuster
new.description: A cone-head streamer with a pine squirrel zonker strip wound as a collar over a tinsel body. Quick to tie and full of movement.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it along banks and through runs; olive, black and natural are the go-to colours.
steps: Add the cone and a few wraps of lead-free wire pushed into it.
Wrap a sparkle braid body.
Tie a squirrel strip on top at the bend, skin side down, and bind it down the shank with the wire rib, Matuka-style.
Wind the rest of the strip two or three turns behind the cone as a collar.
Tie off, whip finish behind the cone.

new.name: Black Ghost
new.description: Maine's famous streamer: yellow hackle tail and throat, black floss body ribbed with silver, white saddle hackle wing.
new.fishing_tips: Troll or strip it for trout and landlocked salmon, especially after ice-out when smelt are running.
steps: Tie in a yellow hackle-fibre tail and the tinsel.
Wrap a slim black floss body and rib with the tinsel.
Tie in a yellow throat under the hook.
Tie four matched white saddle hackles on top as the wing, reaching past the bend.
Add jungle cock cheeks if you have them, build the head, whip finish and varnish.

new.name: Egg Sucking Leech
new.description: A black or purple woolly-bugger-style leech with a bright chenille egg at the head.
new.fishing_tips: Swing it for steelhead and salmon, or strip it for trout below spawning fish.
steps: Tie in a marabou tail as long as the shank.
Tie in a saddle hackle and the body chenille at the bend.
Wind the chenille forward to a quarter shank behind the eye, palmer the hackle through it.
Wind a ball of fluorescent chenille at the front as the egg.
Whip finish.
new.imitates: Leeches with an egg (or an egg being eaten)
new.hatch: Autumn and winter, during and after salmon spawning

new.name: Glo Bug
new.description: A single bright yarn egg, clipped round, often with a contrasting blood dot.
new.fishing_tips: Dead-drift it near the bottom below spawning salmon and trout, or in winter steelhead runs.
steps: Lay a thread base in the middle of the shank.
Tie a bundle of yarn (with a small dot strand on top) straight up with several tight wraps.
Pull the yarn up tight and trim it in one cut, close to the hook.
Fluff it into a round egg and whip finish under it.

new.name: Gotcha
new.description: The best-selling bonefish fly: pink tail, pearl body, tan craft fur wing with flash, and bead chain eyes so it rides hook-up.
new.fishing_tips: Cast it ahead of cruising bonefish, let it sink, then strip short and slow.
mats: Tan craft fur or calf tail, with a few strands of flash
steps: Tie the eyes on top of the shank just behind the eye.
Tie in a short pink flash tail at the bend.
Wrap a pearl braid body forward and tie off behind the eyes.
Turn the hook over and tie a sparse craft fur wing on the other side so it rides hook-point up.
Whip finish in front of the eyes.

new.name: Bendback
new.description: A weedless baitfish tied on a slightly bent hook so it rides point-up: a tinsel body under a bucktail or synthetic wing.
new.fishing_tips: Drag it through grass and mangrove roots for snook, redfish and seatrout without hanging up.
mats: Saltwater hook, bent slightly up near the eye, #2–2/0
Bucktail or synthetic fibre, with flash
steps: Bend the shank up slightly about a third back from the eye.
Wrap a braid body from the bend to the bend in the shank.
Turn the hook over and tie in a sparse wing so it covers the point.
Add flash and stick-on eyes, build a head and coat it with UV resin.

new.name: Catskill Adams
new.description: The original Adams: grizzly hen-tip wings, mixed brown and grizzly tail and hackle, grey muskrat body.
new.fishing_tips: A general grey mayfly; fish it to rising trout on riffles and flats.
steps: Tie in two grizzly hackle tips upright and divided a third back from the eye.
Tie in a mixed brown and grizzly tail.
Dub a slim grey body to the wings.
Wind the two hackles behind and in front of the wings, whip finish.

new.name: Light Cahill
new.description: A pale cream Catskill dry: wood duck wings and tail, cream dubbed body and light ginger hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it at dusk on summer evenings when pale mayflies hatch.
mats: Wood duck flank, upright and divided
steps: Tie in wood duck wings, stand them up and divide them.
Add a ginger tail.
Dub a slim cream body.
Wind the hackle around the wings and whip finish.
new.imitates: Light Cahill and pale summer mayflies (Stenacron, Maccaffertium)

new.name: Hendrickson
new.description: A Catskill dry for the first big mayfly hatch of spring: wood duck wings, pinkish-tan body and dun hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it in early spring afternoons when Hendricksons hatch on eastern rivers.
steps: Tie in wood duck wings, upright and divided.
Add a dun tail.
Dub a tapered pinkish-tan body.
Wind the dun hackle and whip finish.

new.name: Quill Gordon
new.description: Theodore Gordon's classic: wood duck wings, a stripped peacock quill body with clear segments, and dun hackle.
new.fishing_tips: One of the first dries of spring in the East; fish it on cold early-season afternoons.
steps: Tie in the wood duck wings, upright and divided.
Add a dun tail and the stripped quill.
Wind the quill forward in touching turns so the segments show; coat it for strength.
Wind the hackle and whip finish.

new.name: Parachute BWO
new.description: An olive-bodied parachute for Baetis hatches: dun tail, olive dubbing, grey post and dun hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it small on cloudy, drizzly days when blue-winged olives hatch.
steps: Tie in the post and stand it up.
Add the tail and dub a slim olive body.
Tie in the hackle at the post and dub the thorax.
Wind the hackle down the post, tie off and whip finish.

new.name: Parachute PMD
new.description: A pale yellow parachute for Pale Morning Dun hatches on western rivers.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it to selective trout during PMD hatches on summer mornings and afternoons.
steps: Tie in the post.
Add the tail and dub a slim yellow body.
Tie in the hackle, dub the thorax, wind the parachute.
Whip finish.

new.name: Humpy
new.creator_name: Western classic (also called the Goofus Bug)
new.description: A super-buoyant attractor: a deer hair shellback over a floss underbody, with hair tips forming the wings.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it in fast pocket water where you need a fly that will not sink.
mats: Deer hair pulled over floss underbody
steps: Tie in a moose tail.
Tie in a bunch of deer hair, tips back, measured so the tips will become the wings.
Build a floss underbody, pull the hair over it and tie down.
Stand the hair tips up as divided wings.
Wind the hackles and whip finish.
new.imitates: General attractor; mayflies and caddis in fast water

new.name: Irresistible
new.description: A dry with a spun and clipped deer hair body, so it floats like a cork in rough water.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it in heavy riffles and pocket water.
mats: Grizzly hackle tips or calf hair
steps: Tie in the tail.
Spin several bunches of deer hair over the rear two-thirds, packing them tight.
Clip the hair to a tapered body.
Tie in the wings, wind the hackles and whip finish.

new.name: Renegade
new.description: A fore-and-aft hackled fly: brown hackle at the back, white at the front, and a peacock herl body.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it dry or let it sink and swing it as a wet fly.
steps: Wrap a small gold tinsel tag.
Wind a brown hackle at the rear.
Wrap a peacock herl body.
Wind a white hackle at the front and whip finish.
new.imitates: General attractor; suggests beetles and caddis

new.name: H&L Variant
new.description: A high-floating attractor with white calf wings, a split body of stripped quill and peacock herl, and brown hackle.
new.fishing_tips: A visible searching dry for fast mountain streams.
mats: Stripped peacock quill rear, peacock herl front
steps: Tie in white calf wings, upright and divided.
Add a calf tail.
Wrap a stripped quill rear body and a peacock herl front body.
Wind the hackle and whip finish.

new.name: Trico Spinner
new.description: A tiny spent spinner: black thorax, white abdomen and white poly wings lying flat in the film.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it on summer mornings during the Trico spinner fall, with a long fine tippet.
steps: Tie in a split tail.
Wrap a slim white abdomen.
Tie in a poly wing crosswise with figure-eight wraps.
Dub a small black thorax around the wings and whip finish.

new.name: Rusty Spinner
new.description: A rust-brown spent spinner with clear or white poly wings.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it in the evening when spent mayflies lie in the film.
steps: Tie in a split tail.
Dub a slim rust body.
Tie in the spent wings with figure-eights.
Dub over the wing base and whip finish.

new.name: Mosquito
new.description: A traditional grey dry with a moose-hair-ribbed body, grizzly tips for wings and grizzly hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Great on northern lakes and streams when mosquitoes and small grey insects are about.
mats: Stripped moose mane, light and dark
steps: Tie in grizzly tip wings.
Add a grizzly tail.
Wrap a striped body of light and dark moose mane hairs.
Wind the grizzly hackle and whip finish.

new.name: Foam Ant
new.description: Two humps of black foam with a brown hackle in the middle and a small indicator on top.
new.fishing_tips: Drop it along grassy banks and under trees on summer afternoons; trout rarely refuse an ant.
mats: Orange or pink foam or yarn
steps: Tie a foam strip in at the bend and fold it forward to form the rear hump.
Tie it down at mid-shank and wind two turns of hackle there.
Fold the foam forward again to form the front hump and tie off.
Add an indicator on top and whip finish.

new.name: Dave's Hopper
new.description: Dave Whitlock's classic hopper: red deer hair tail, yellow body palmered and clipped, turkey wing, knotted legs and a spun deer hair head.
new.fishing_tips: Slap it down by grassy banks on breezy summer afternoons.
mats: Yellow yarn loop and yellow poly, palmered brown hackle clipped
steps: Tie in a red deer hair tail and a short yarn loop extension.
Wrap a yarn body palmered with brown hackle; clip the hackle short.
Tie in a turkey wing and knotted legs.
Spin deer hair for the collar and head, clip to shape, whip finish.

new.name: Morrish Hopper
new.description: A modern foam hopper: a layered foam body cut to shape, rubber legs and an elk or poly wing.
new.fishing_tips: Bombs it into the banks and it floats all day; a great dropper carrier.
steps: Cut and glue a two-colour foam body.
Tie it down at the rear and front segments.
Add the wing and legs at the front segment.
Whip finish under the foam.

new.name: Yellow Sally
new.description: A small yellow stonefly adult: yellow dubbed body, a flat wing and light hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it on summer evenings when little yellow stoneflies are egg-laying.
mats: Yellow dubbing with a red butt
Light elk hair or poly, flat
steps: Dub a small red butt then a slim yellow body.
Tie a flat wing on top.
Wind the hackle and whip finish.

new.name: Goddard Caddis
new.description: A spun and clipped deer hair caddis shaped like a tent, with a brown hackle and antennae. Practically unsinkable.
new.fishing_tips: Skate it across a riffle or a lake in the evening.
mats: Spun deer hair, clipped to a tent shape
steps: Spin deer hair over most of the shank.
Clip it into a caddis tent shape, flat underneath.
Tie in two hackle-stem antennae and wind the hackle in front.
Whip finish.

new.name: X-Caddis
new.description: An emerging caddis: a Z-Lon trailing shuck, dubbed body and a deer hair wing with no hackle, sitting low in the film.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it to fussy trout eating caddis emergers in the film.
steps: Tie in a short Z-Lon shuck.
Dub a slim body.
Tie in a stacked deer hair wing, flaring it slightly.
Trim the butts to a head and whip finish.

new.name: Purple Haze
new.description: A Parachute Adams with a purple body, which trout seem to find irresistible.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it like an Adams on western rivers; the purple helps in low light.
steps: Tie in the post.
Add the tail and dub a purple body.
Tie in the hackles, dub the thorax, wind the parachute.
Whip finish.

new.name: Klinkhamer Special
new.description: A parachute emerger on a curved hook: the abdomen hangs below the film while the thorax and hackle float.
new.fishing_tips: Excellent for selective trout and grayling during caddis and mayfly hatches.
steps: Tie in a poly post at the front, angled forward.
Dub a slim abdomen well round the bend.
Wrap a peacock herl thorax.
Wind the parachute hackle and whip finish.

new.name: Perdigon
new.description: A slim, heavy, smooth nymph: Coq de Leon tail, thread body coated in UV resin and a tungsten bead. Sinks like a stone.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it on a Euro rig in fast, deep runs where you need to get down quickly.
mats: Thread with a holographic tinsel rib
Black marker or a hot-spot thread band
steps: Add the bead and tie in a Coq de Leon tail.
Wrap a slim, tapered thread body and rib it with fine tinsel.
Colour a wing case on top or add a hot-spot thread band.
Coat the whole body with thin UV resin and cure it.

new.name: Rainbow Warrior
new.description: A flashy pearl-backed nymph: a red thread base under a pearl tinsel body and a rainbow-dubbed thorax.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it as an attractor dropper in tailwaters and riffles.
steps: Add the bead and tie in a short pheasant tail tail and pearl tinsel.
Build a red thread base and pull the pearl over the top.
Dub a rainbow thorax and pull the pearl over as a wing case.
Whip finish.
new.imitates: Attractor; suggests midge pupae and Baetis nymphs

new.name: Lightning Bug
new.description: A flash nymph: a pearl or silver tinsel body, pheasant tail tail and a peacock thorax with a flashback.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it as a dropper in clear water; the flash draws strikes.
mats: Peacock herl or dubbing with a flashback
steps: Add the bead and tie in the tail.
Wrap a smooth tinsel body.
Wrap the thorax and pull a flashback over.
Whip finish.

new.name: Juju Baetis
new.description: A slim Baetis nymph with a two-tone thread abdomen, a flashback wing case and CDC or fibre legs.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it as the dropper during and before a BWO hatch.
mats: Two colours of thread twisted together
steps: Tie in a short tail.
Wrap a slim segmented abdomen of two twisted threads.
Tie in the wing case materials and dub a small thorax.
Pull the wing case over, add legs, whip finish.

new.name: Two Bit Hooker
new.description: A heavy little mayfly nymph with two tungsten beads, a pheasant tail body and a peacock thorax.
new.fishing_tips: Use it to get a small nymph down fast in deep, quick water.
steps: Slide on two beads.
Tie in the tail and wrap a ribbed pheasant body.
Wrap a little thorax between the beads.
Whip finish behind the front bead.

new.name: Scud
new.description: A curved, segmented freshwater shrimp: dubbed body under a clear shellback, ribbed with wire or mono.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it slowly near weed beds in spring creeks, tailwaters and lakes.
mats: Olive, tan or pink dubbing, picked out
steps: Add a few wraps of weight and a short tail.
Tie in the shellback and rib.
Dub a full body and pick out the underside for legs.
Pull the shellback over, rib through it and whip finish.

new.name: Sow Bug
new.description: A flat, grey cressbug: a wide dubbed body under a Thin Skin back, ribbed for segments.
new.fishing_tips: Dead-drift it in spring creeks and tailwaters with weed beds.
mats: Grey rabbit or sow bug dubbing, picked out
steps: Tie in the back material and rib at the bend.
Dub a broad, flat grey body.
Pull the back over, rib it and whip finish; pick out the sides.
new.hatch: All year on spring creeks and tailwaters

new.name: Breadcrust
new.description: An old caddis larva pattern with a body wrapped from a stripped ruffed grouse tail quill and a grizzly collar.
new.fishing_tips: Dead-drift it near the bottom when caddis larvae are active.
steps: Build a tapered orange underbody.
Wind the stripped quill over it so the orange shows between turns.
Wind two turns of grizzly hen and whip finish.

new.name: Kaufmann's Stone
new.description: A big, realistic stonefly nymph: biot tails and antennae, a dubbed body with a Swiss straw back, and segmented wing cases.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it deep in fast western rivers before and during the salmonfly and golden stone hatches.
mats: Turkey or Thin Skin, three sections
steps: Weight and flatten the shank, tie in biot tails.
Tie in the back and rib, dub the abdomen, pull the back over and rib it.
Build the thorax in three sections, each with a wing case folded over.
Add biot antennae, form the head and whip finish.
new.hatch: All year; peak in late spring

new.name: Golden Stone Nymph
new.description: A golden-brown stonefly nymph with a mottled back, rubber or biot legs, and a weighted, flattened body.
new.fishing_tips: Bounce it along the bottom in riffles in early summer.
steps: Weight the shank and tie in the biot tails.
Build the abdomen under a mottled back.
Form the thorax with legs and wing cases.
Add antennae and whip finish.

new.name: Bitch Creek Nymph
new.description: A weighted stonefly with a woven black-and-orange chenille body, rubber legs and tails, and a palmered hackle thorax.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it deep in fast western rivers; bass and bluegills like it too.
steps: Weight the shank and tie in rubber tails.
Weave a body of black (top) and orange (belly) chenille.
Wind a black chenille thorax with a brown hackle palmered through it.
Add rubber antennae and whip finish.

new.name: Squirmy Wormy
new.description: A stretchy silicone 'squirmy' worm tied on with a bead so it wiggles with every drift.
new.fishing_tips: Deadly in high, coloured water and stocked rivers; banned on some fly-only waters, so check the rules.
steps: Slide on the bead and start the thread behind it.
Tie the silicone strand on top at its middle with a few light but firm wraps.
Wrap a small thread collar to lock it, whip finish and add a drop of glue.

new.name: Mop Fly
new.description: A single chunk of microfibre mop tied behind a bead. Looks like a caddis larva, grub or stocker pellet.
new.fishing_tips: Dead-drift it in stocked rivers and high water; controversial but effective.
steps: Add the bead.
Tie in a mop finger along the shank, tapering the end.
Dub a small collar behind the bead and whip finish; glue the tie-in point.

new.name: Green Rock Worm
new.description: A bright green free-living caddis larva: a segmented green body with a dark head and a few short legs.
new.fishing_tips: Bounce it along the bottom in fast riffles; Rhyacophila are common in freestone streams.
mats: Bright green dubbing or Ultra Chenille
steps: Weight the shank and tie in the rib.
Dub a segmented green body around the bend.
Add a few partridge fibres underneath and dub a dark head.
Whip finish.
new.hatch: All year; spring and autumn emergence

new.name: LaFontaine Sparkle Pupa
new.description: Gary LaFontaine's caddis pupa: an Antron sheath trapping air bubbles over a dubbed body, with a deer hair wing and dubbed head.
new.fishing_tips: Swing it up through the water or dead-drift it in the film during caddis hatches.
steps: Tie in strands of Antron above and below the bend.
Dub the underbody, pull the Antron loosely over it to form a bubble sheath and tie off.
Add a sparse deer hair wing.
Dub a head and whip finish.

new.name: Disco Midge
new.description: A tiny pearl midge: a pearl Krystal Flash body and a peacock herl head.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it as the trailing fly on tailwaters in winter.
steps: Tie in a strand of Krystal Flash and wrap a slim body.
Wind one peacock herl for the head.
Whip finish.

new.name: Brassie
new.description: A copper wire midge larva with a dark dubbed head. Heavy for its size.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it deep in tailwaters and slow runs.
steps: Tie in the copper wire and wind a smooth body.
Dub a small dark head.
Whip finish.

new.name: Mercury Midge
new.description: A midge pupa with a silver-lined glass bead head that looks like a trapped air bubble.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it near the surface or mid-depth when midges are hatching.
steps: Slide on the glass bead.
Wrap a slim thread body and rib it with wire.
Whip finish behind the bead.

new.name: Top Secret Midge
new.description: A tiny emerging midge with a thread body, a dubbed thorax and a short white Z-Lon wing.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it in the film to sipping trout on tailwaters.
steps: Wrap a ribbed thread abdomen.
Tie in a short Z-Lon wing tuft.
Dub a small thorax and whip finish.

new.name: WD-40
new.description: A simple midge or Baetis emerger: wood duck tail, a thread abdomen and a dubbed thorax under a wood duck wing case.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it as a dropper in tailwaters; very effective in winter.
mats: Wood duck or mallard flank fibres
steps: Tie in wood duck fibres as a tail, keeping the butts.
Wrap a thread abdomen.
Dub a thorax, pull the fibre butts over it as a wing case.
Whip finish.

new.name: Barr's Emerger
new.description: A Baetis/PMD emerger that hangs in the film: brown fibre tail, slim abdomen, and a dun hackle-fibre wing case over a dubbed thorax.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it as a dropper just under the surface during mayfly hatches.
steps: Tie in a short tail.
Dub a slim abdomen.
Tie in dun fibres for the wing case, dub the thorax.
Pull the fibres over, fold the tips back as legs, whip finish.

new.name: Psycho Prince
new.description: A modern, colourful Prince: tinsel-ribbed body with a flashy back, coloured biot wings and a bead.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it as an attractor nymph; works well on steelhead tributaries too.
steps: Add the bead, tie in a biot tail.
Build the body.
Tie in biot wings on top, flared.
Dub a collar and whip finish.

new.name: Partridge & Green
new.description: A sparse soft hackle: green silk body, sometimes with a hare's ear thorax, and one or two turns of partridge.
new.fishing_tips: Swing it down and across or let it drift in riffles during caddis and mayfly hatches.
steps: Wrap a slim green silk body.
Add a pinch of hare's ear dubbing for a thorax.
Wind one or two turns of partridge and whip finish.

new.name: Zonker
new.description: A rabbit strip streamer: a Mylar tube body with a full zonker strip tied down on top and a hackle collar.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it with pauses so the rabbit breathes; a big-trout and bass fly.
steps: Build a short tapered underbody and slide Mylar tubing over it; tie down both ends.
Tie a zonker strip on at the bend and again behind the eye, skin side down.
Wind a hackle collar, whip finish and coat the head.

new.name: Bunny Leech
new.description: A rabbit strip tail and a wound rabbit strip body: about the simplest, most lively leech there is.
new.fishing_tips: Strip or twitch it near the bottom; black, olive and purple.
steps: Tie in a rabbit strip tail.
Wind a second rabbit strip forward, stroking the fur back each turn.
Whip finish.

new.name: Thin Mint
new.description: A woolly bugger with a mixed brown-and-olive marabou tail, peacock-and-black body and a bead head.
new.fishing_tips: Strip or dead-drift it in rivers and lakes.
mats: Black, olive and brown marabou with flash
steps: Add the bead and tie in a mixed marabou tail.
Tie in hackle and chenille, wind the body, palmer the hackle.
Whip finish behind the bead.

new.name: Autumn Splendor
new.description: A Colorado classic bugger: brown and yellow marabou tail, orange-brown chenille body, rubber legs and a cone head.
new.fishing_tips: A great big-brown-trout fly in autumn.
mats: Brown and yellow marabou with flash
steps: Add the cone and tie in the marabou tail.
Wind the chenille body and palmer the hackle.
Tie rubber legs at the front and whip finish.

new.name: Kreelex
new.description: An all-flash minnow: gold and silver Flashabou layered over the hook with stick-on eyes.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it fast for smallmouth and trout in clear rivers.
mats: Gold and silver Flashabou, tied both sides
steps: Tie a bunch of silver Flashabou on top and bottom, then gold on top.
Fold forward-facing bunches back for a fuller head.
Glue on the eyes and coat the head.

new.name: Matuka
new.description: A wing of hackle feathers bound down along the body with wire, so it can't foul around the hook.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it slowly near the bottom; it imitates bullies, sculpins and small fish.
mats: Four matched hen or saddle hackles
steps: Tie in the rib and wind the body.
Strip the underside of the hackles and lay them on top as the wing.
Bind the wing down with the rib, working the wire through the fibres.
Wind a collar and whip finish.

new.name: Gray Ghost
new.description: Carrie Stevens' famous featherwing streamer with a gray saddle wing, orange floss body and golden pheasant shoulders.
new.fishing_tips: Troll or strip it for landlocked salmon and brook trout, especially early in the season when smelt run.
mats: Four gray saddle hackles over golden pheasant crest
steps: Wrap an orange floss body and rib it with silver.
Tie in the belly materials under the hook.
Tie in a golden pheasant crest and four gray saddles as the wing.
Add the shoulders and cheeks, build a neat head, whip finish and varnish.

new.name: Black Nosed Dace
new.description: Art Flick's minnow streamer: a silver body with a white, black and brown bucktail wing in three layers.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it along the bottom where real dace live.
steps: Tie in a short red tail and wrap a silver body.
Stack the wing: white bucktail, then black, then brown on top.
Build the head and whip finish.

new.name: Sparkle Minnow
new.description: A flashy cone-head minnow with a sparkle braid body and a marabou tail.
new.fishing_tips: Strip or swing it in rivers for smallmouth and trout.
steps: Add the cone and tie in the tail.
Wrap the braid body.
Whip finish behind the cone.

new.name: Meat Whistle
new.description: A jig-style rabbit strip streamer with a cone, rubber legs and flash. Rides point-up and swims like a crayfish or sculpin.
new.fishing_tips: Hop it along the bottom for bass and trout.
steps: Add the cone and wrap a short body.
Tie a rabbit strip on top as the tail.
Add flash, legs and a marabou collar.
Whip finish behind the cone.

new.name: Green Butt Skunk
new.description: A black steelhead fly with a fluorescent green butt, red tail, silver rib and white calf tail wing.
new.fishing_tips: Swing it on summer and winter steelhead runs.
steps: Tie in a red tail and wind a short green butt.
Wrap a black body and rib it.
Add a black throat hackle and a white calf wing.
Build the head and whip finish.

new.name: Polar Shrimp
new.description: A fluorescent orange steelhead fly with a red tail, orange hackle and white wing.
new.fishing_tips: A bright fly for coloured or cold water.
mats: White calf tail or polar bear substitute
steps: Tie in the tail.
Wind the orange chenille body.
Add the hackle and white wing.
Whip finish.

new.name: Silver Hilton
new.description: A black-and-silver steelhead fly with a mallard tail, grizzly hackle-tip wings and grizzly hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Swing it on summer steelhead rivers.
steps: Tie in a mallard tail.
Wrap the black body and rib it.
Add the hackle and grizzly tip wings.
Whip finish.

new.name: Comet
new.description: A weighted fly with a long fluorescent tail, tinsel body, hackle collar and bead chain eyes.
new.fishing_tips: Drift or swing it deep for steelhead and salmon.
mats: Orange bucktail or calf tail, long
steps: Tie on the eyes.
Tie in a long tail.
Wrap a tinsel body.
Wind the hackle behind the eyes and whip finish.

new.name: Rusty Rat
new.creator_name: Rat series (Roy Angus Thomson); Rusty Rat by J. Kenneth Ross
new.description: A famous Atlantic salmon hairwing: half rusty floss and half peacock body, grey squirrel wing and grizzly collar.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it on a floating line in summer.
mats: Rusty orange floss (rear) and peacock herl (front)
steps: Wrap the tag and tie in a peacock sword tail.
Wrap the two-part body and rib it.
Tie in a grey squirrel wing.
Wind the grizzly collar and whip finish.

new.name: Blue Charm
new.description: A traditional low-water salmon fly: black body ribbed silver, blue throat, mallard wing over a golden pheasant tail.
new.fishing_tips: A summer low-water fly; fish it small near the surface.
steps: Wrap the tag and tie in the tail.
Wrap the black body and rib it.
Add a blue throat.
Tie in the wing, build the head and whip finish.

new.name: Bomber
new.description: A floating Atlantic salmon fly: a spun and clipped deer hair body palmered with hackle, and a calf tail tail and horn.
new.fishing_tips: Wake it across the surface or dead-drift it for salmon and steelhead.
steps: Tie in the tail.
Spin deer hair along the shank and clip it into a cigar.
Palmer the hackle through the hair.
Tie in a forward-pointing horn and whip finish.

new.name: Surf Candy
new.description: A slim, translucent baitfish coated in epoxy or UV resin, with stick-on eyes. Durable against teeth.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it fast through bait schools for albies, bluefish, stripers and Spanish mackerel.
mats: Ultra Hair or bucktail in layers
steps: Wrap a pearl body.
Tie the wing in layers, light below and dark on top.
Add the eyes and coat the front half in resin.
Shape and cure.

new.name: Half and Half
new.description: A Clouser Minnow front with a Deceiver's saddle-hackle tail: a longer baitfish that still jigs.
new.fishing_tips: Use it for stripers, snook and redfish when you need a bigger profile that gets down.
mats: Bucktail in two colours, with flash
steps: Tie on dumbbell eyes and a saddle hackle tail.
Tie white bucktail in front of the eyes and pull it back.
Turn the hook over and add flash and the top colour of bucktail.
Whip finish and coat the head.

new.name: Kwan
new.description: A simple weedless redfish fly: a flared deer hair or rabbit tail, a chenille body and dumbbell eyes so it rides point-up.
new.fishing_tips: Hop it slowly in front of tailing or cruising redfish.
steps: Tie on the eyes.
Tie in a fur tail.
Wind the body and add legs.
Whip finish.

new.name: Cockroach
new.description: A classic tarpon fly with a splayed grizzly saddle tail and a grey squirrel or bucktail collar.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it slow and steady in front of rolling or laid-up tarpon.
steps: Tie in a splayed grizzly tail at the bend.
Tie a collar of grey squirrel around the shank.
Build a long thread head and coat it.

new.name: Black Death
new.description: A black-and-red tarpon fly: black saddle hackles splayed at the tail and a red hackle collar.
new.fishing_tips: A low-light and dirty-water tarpon fly.
steps: Tie in the black saddles at the bend.
Wind a red hackle collar.
Build the head and coat it.

new.name: Apte Tarpon Fly
new.description: Stu Apte's classic: orange and yellow splayed saddle tail with an orange hackle collar.
new.fishing_tips: A bright tarpon fly for clear water and sunny days.
steps: Tie in the saddles at the bend, splayed out.
Wind the collar hackle.
Build and coat the head.

new.name: Critter Crab
new.description: A small crab: a spun and clipped deer hair or yarn body with rubber legs and lead eyes, so it dives and rests on the bottom.
new.fishing_tips: Drop it in front of tailing bonefish, redfish or permit and let it sit.
mats: Spun deer hair or yarn, clipped flat
steps: Tie on the eyes and the claws.
Spin or tie a body, clipping it into a flat crab shape.
Add rubber legs and whip finish.

new.name: Dahlberg Diver
new.description: A spun deer hair diver with a flat collar that makes it dive and wobble when stripped, and float back up when paused.
new.fishing_tips: Strip, pause, strip around weed beds and lily pads.
mats: Spun deer hair, clipped with a diving collar
steps: Tie in the marabou and flash tail.
Spin deer hair over the front half, packing tightly.
Clip a flat face and a flared collar.
Whip finish and add a weedguard.

new.name: Crayfish
new.description: A weighted crayfish with rabbit or hackle claws, a dubbed body under a back and rubber legs, tied to ride point-up.
new.fishing_tips: Hop it slowly along rocky bottoms for bass, and for carp and trout too.
steps: Tie the eyes so the fly rides point-up.
Tie in the claws and feelers at the bend.
Dub the body with legs and pull a back over it, ribbing for segments.
Whip finish.

new.name: Sneaky Pete
new.description: A foam or cork slider with a bullet-shaped head that pushes a gentle wake instead of popping.
new.fishing_tips: Twitch it gently for wary bass and big bluegills.
steps: Tie in a tail and legs.
Glue the slider head on the shank, narrow end forward.
Let it set before fishing.

new.name: Murdich Minnow
new.description: A durable synthetic baitfish with a flash body and a long synthetic wing, built for stripers and bass.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it fast through bait.
steps: Wrap a flash body.
Tie in the wing in layers.
Add eyes and coat the head.

new.name: Wooly Worm
new.description: The older cousin of the Woolly Bugger: a red yarn tail, chenille body and a palmered grizzly hackle.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it slowly for panfish and trout.
steps: Tie in a short red tail.
Tie in the hackle and chenille, wind the body.
Palmer the hackle forward and whip finish.

new.name: Crappie Jig Fly
new.description: A marabou and chenille jig fly with a bead head that swims like a little jig.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it slowly under a float or count it down near brush piles.
steps: Add the bead and tie in the marabou tail.
Wind a chenille body.
Whip finish.

new.name: Carp Carrot
new.description: An orange-and-green fly that looks a bit like a crayfish or nymph; a long-time carp favourite.
new.fishing_tips: Drop it in front of feeding carp and twitch it slightly.
steps: Tie on the eyes.
Wind an orange chenille body.
Add an olive tuft and whip finish.

new.name: Clouser Swimming Nymph
new.description: A weighted nymph with a marabou tail and a dubbed body under a shellback; it swims like a damsel or dragonfly nymph.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it slowly near the bottom for smallmouth, carp and trout.
steps: Weight the shank and tie in a marabou tail.
Dub the abdomen.
Tie in the shellback and hackle, dub the thorax, palmer the hackle.
Pull the shellback over and whip finish.

new.name: Pike Bunny Fly
new.description: A long rabbit strip with flash and a wound rabbit collar on a strong hook. Simple, cheap and deadly.
new.fishing_tips: Strip it with long pauses; always use a bite tippet.
steps: Tie in a long zonker strip tail with flash.
Wind a rabbit collar forward.
Add eyes and whip finish.

new.name: Shad Fly
new.description: A small flashy fly with bead chain eyes, a short tail and a tinsel body, for spring shad runs.
new.fishing_tips: Swing it through runs and riffles during the spring shad run.
steps: Tie on the eyes.
Tie in a short tail and wrap the tinsel body.
Wind a small chenille collar and whip finish.
